{"lessons": ["

The Italian meal

An Italian menu always follows the same order. Knowing it already means understanding half of what the waiter says.

On the menuWhat it is
l'antipastothe starter: cold cuts, vegetables, bruschette
il primopasta, risotto or soup
il secondomeat or fish
il contornothe side dish, ordered separately
il dolcedessert

The trap: il secondo arrives alone on the plate. If you want vegetables or potatoes, you have to order un contorno.

On the bill at most restaurants, il coperto is a fixed amount per person for the place setting and the bread. It is not a tip.

", "

Useful phrases

WhenWhat you say
ArrivingAvete un tavolo per due?
OrderingVorrei… / Per me… / Prendo…
HesitatingChe cosa mi consiglia?
AskingMi porta il menù, per favore?
WarningSono allergico a…
PayingIl conto, per favore.

To order, vorrei (I would like) is the polite phrase. Per me (for me) and prendo (I'll have, literally \"I take\") are just as natural. With the waiter, you use the formal Lei: \"Mi porta dell'acqua?\"

Some bread, some water, some potatoes

For an unspecified quantity, Italian uses di + the article, where English says \"some\" or nothing at all. These are the articulated prepositions you already know.

Vorrei del pane, della frutta e delle patate.I'd like some bread, some fruit and some potatoes.

Before a vowel: dell' (dell'acqua). In the masculine plural: dei (dei funghi).
